strings.guide.fab.title: Walkthrough Guide
strings.guide.fast.d: When requirements are early and function points cannot be broken down yet, count ILF / EIF with the NESMA predictive or estimated method to get a size and cost magnitude instantly.
strings.guide.fast_count.d: Enter ILF / EIF (plus EI / EO / EQ in estimated mode) for the selected method; results recalculate as you type.
strings.guide.fast_gb.d: Click Use this result in GB cost to carry the current UFP into the GB/T 36964 tab on the result page.
strings.guide.help.d: Upload the requirements document → review function points → generate the cost table: this is the main workflow.
strings.guide.help_config.d: Configure LLM-assisted recognition (provider / API URL / key) and the application update source, with an online connection test.
strings.guide.help_doc.d: Read the methodology and calculation notes of every module, and replay any page's walkthrough from here.
strings.guide.help_fast.d: NESMA quick estimate: count ILF / EIF and get size and cost instantly — ideal for early-stage sizing.
strings.guide.help_pert.d: Three-point estimation: enter optimistic / most likely / pessimistic values and get the expected duration and variance automatically.
strings.guide.pert.d: The PERT estimate is organised in three steps — Input, Effort Entry and Result — each with its own step bar.
strings.guide.pert_edit.d: Maintain the per-phase items during Effort Entry; load a previous project here to keep editing it.
strings.guide.pert_gen.d: The Result step outputs the expected effort per phase and lets you download the finished table.
strings.guide.pert_in.d: Enter the three-point values for each requirement: optimistic (O), most likely (M) and pessimistic (P); the system computes the expected duration and variance.
strings.guide.work.d: Drag a requirements document in, or click to choose one (.docx). The local engine parses it and produces the IFPUG candidate function points — step 1 of the IFPUG estimate.
strings.guide.work_result.d: Step 3 “Result and download” summarises effort and cost, and exports the finished cost table (Excel) in one click.
strings.guide.work_review.d: Recognition results land in step 2 “Review function points”, where you can tick or adjust each function point’s type and reuse level, then confirm to run the estimate.
strings.guide.work_upload.d: Drop the requirements file onto the dashed frame here, or click it to open the file picker.
strings.help.body.a1: For a single function point: UFP = default type weight (ILF 10 / EIF 7 / EI 4 / EO 5 / EQ 4); the predictive function point method uses ILF=35 and EIF=15 only, with transactional types falling back to the estimated weights.
strings.help.body.a2f: US = UFP × Reuse Factor × Modification Factor
strings.help.body.a3f: Adjusted size = ΣUS × Size Changing Adjustment Factor
strings.help.body.a3t: (1.39 early / 1.21 mid / 1.10 late / 1.00 post-delivery and O&M)
strings.help.body.a4f: Effort (person-days) = Adjusted size × Productivity (person-hours/FP) ÷ 8 × Adjustment Factor 0.8
strings.help.body.a4t: Low / medium / high take the mid-value ±20% as bounds.
strings.help.body.a5f: Cost = Effort (person-days) ÷ 22 × Cost per Person-Month (10k CNY)
strings.help.body.a5t: The cost per person-month defaults to 2.57 (10k CNY) and is editable in the project parameters.
strings.help.body.a6: The mid-value ±20% forms the lower/upper bound for negotiation-range reference.
strings.help.body.c1: Connect any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenAI / Claude / Qwen / Volcano / Agnes / custom presets). Fill in the API URL, model name and key; connection test, model-list fetch, console jump and reset-to-default are supported. The key is stored only in the local data/config.json. When enabled, the model cross-checks and completes candidate function points; connection errors or timeouts fall back to local rules automatically.
strings.help.body.c3: Rules match from high to low priority; the first hit decides the type. Multiple regular expressions and exclusions are supported. Saved changes take effect on the next recognition and record a rule version.
strings.help.body.c4: Maintain multiple yearly rate versions (PDR, person-month rate, function point unit price, direct non-labor cost and data source); the selected version is used and recorded during estimation.
strings.help.body.c5: Upload a new finished-table template and register its basis notes; after uploading, generate a first copy and check the column alignment manually. Formula cache can run in the background, synchronously at generation time, or be turned off, with a timeout guard.
strings.help.body.c6: After setting the update-source JSON URL under Application update, the app checks automatically at startup and when Help is opened; a new version can be downloaded and installed in one click while keeping local configuration. The operations area exports diagnostic bundles and exports/imports all data (a backup is taken before import).
strings.help.body.f1: When requirements are still early and function points cannot be broken down yet, just count ILF / EIF (plus EI / EO / EQ in estimated mode) and get a size and cost magnitude instantly.
strings.help.body.f2est: Estimated method: UFP = 7 × ILF + 5 × EIF + 4 × EI + 5 × EO + 4 × EQ
strings.help.body.f3: The page instantly returns UFP, size (UFP × requirement-stage adjustment factor 1.10), effort (PDR × size) and cost (effort ÷ 174 × person-month rate + direct non-labor cost), together with COCOMO II and PERT three-point references.
strings.help.body.f4: Click Use this result in GB cost to carry the current UFP into the GB/T 36964 tab on the result page.
strings.help.body.g1: The GB Cost tab on the result page follows GB/T 36964-2018: size = UFP × GSC × stage factor CF; effort AE = PDR × size × business-domain factor SWF × language factor RDF; cost = AE ÷ 174 × person-month rate + direct non-labor cost. Custom overrides of benchmark values are marked as Manually adjusted.
strings.help.body.g2: On the result page, confirmed function points become INVEST-template user stories (with acceptance criteria and size); edit them, export Markdown / CSV, or push to GitHub Issues in one click (repository and token are user-provided).
strings.help.body.g3: The result page exports the function point detail CSV, a Markdown summary and the assessment report PDF (save-as via the print pipeline).
strings.help.body.g4: Four themes (light / dark / high contrast / follow system), Chinese and English UI, and a custom brand color that also applies to exported headers.
strings.help.body.g5: Computation, storage and UI assets are all local; requirement documents never leave this machine. The LLM API key is stored only in the local configuration file.
strings.help.body.m1b: IFPUG international function point counting standard
strings.help.body.m1c: (Counting Practices Manual); effort and cost are then converted from benchmark data.
strings.help.body.m2.ei: External Input: processing that brings data into the system
strings.help.body.m2.eif: External Interface File: data referenced but maintained outside this system
strings.help.body.m2.eo: External Output: processing that sends data out of the system
strings.help.body.m2.eq: External Inquiry: retrieval-only queries with no business processing
strings.help.body.m2.ilf: Internal Logical File: data files maintained by this system
strings.help.body.m3: Complexity is recorded as Low / Medium / High for reference only and does not affect UFP; the master template has no complexity column and computes UFP with the default type weights: ILF 10, EIF 7, EI 4, EO 5, EQ 4.
strings.help.body.m3b: The predictive FP method counts ILF (35) and EIF (15) only; transactional types fall back to the estimated function point weights.
strings.help.body.m4.reuse_t: : high 1/3, medium 2/3, low 1 (reused functions are not counted at full value)
strings.help.body.m5: On the IFPUG Estimate page, upload a requirements document (.docx — drag it in, click to choose, or press Enter when focused). The local engine parses it into candidate function points. In Review function points, confirm each item's type, complexity, reuse and modification type; search, filter, sort, batch-set and pasting Excel rows are supported. Once every row is confirmed, click Confirm & generate results, then download the finished table on the result page.
strings.help.body.m6: History lets you reopen an estimate to keep editing, save it as a new record or delete it; tick two estimates to diff them item by item. On the result page you can export the function point detail CSV, a Markdown summary and the assessment report PDF, and generate user stories from INVEST.
strings.help.body.p1: PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) suits change/iteration scenarios where requirements are uncertain and function points are hard to count precisely; experts draw on experience to estimate effort directly with three-point values.
strings.help.body.p2.m_t: : the most probable duration under normal conditions (template column E 'Most Likely')
strings.help.body.p2.o_t: : the shortest duration if everything goes smoothly (template column F 'Minimum')
strings.help.body.p2.p_t: : the longest duration including risks (template column G 'Maximum')
strings.help.body.p3b: Input (create or pick a project, upload Word/PDF or paste text; AI splitting or local analysis follows your settings; tick candidates to import) → Effort entry (maintain phase and the three values per item, with expected value and σ shown live) → Result (total expected person-days, ideal person-months, adjustment coefficient and actual estimated person-months, then generate the finished table). Projects are stored in the local SQLite database (data/pert.db) and can be reopened at any time.
strings.help.body.p4a: Expected person-days are aggregated by phase (requirements / design / development / implementation / shared & remote / on-site maintenance)
strings.help.body.p4c_a: Adjustment coefficients (customer 0.06 / quality 0.06 / change 0.05 / schedule 0.06) are added to get the
strings.help.body.p5: Development-phase details are written from row R8 of the output sheet (columns B/C merged; only column D description plus the E/F/G three values); other phases go to their phase rows. Column H expected values are recalculated automatically by template formulas.
strings.help.body.p6a: On the Input step, upload a requirement document (Word/PDF) or paste text, then click 'Upload & Recognize' on the right to start recognition (greyed out until a file is uploaded). The system routes automatically by the
strings.help.body.p6c: switch: when enabled, AI splits functions/work items and gives optimistic / most likely / pessimistic effort for each; when disabled, local offline analysis is used. Tick items to confirm and continue to effort entry.
strings.help.body.p7c: ; during AI estimation its tech stack, structure, dependencies and size are scanned and injected into the prompt as project-level context, making the effort estimate fit the real code.
strings.help.body.p7d: Only metadata such as tech stack, directory structure and dependencies is scanned — business source code is not read. If the directory is missing or unset, the AI skips this context.
strings.help.body.p8a: AI splitting and estimation require enabling the LLM in
strings.help.body.p8c: and filling in the API base URL and key
strings.help.body.p8d: When the LLM is unavailable, docx requirements fall back to local recognition (description only; fill in the three values manually)
strings.help.body.p8e: The project context directory is optional; when unset, AI skips that context without affecting the main flow
strings.help.body.p9a: The PERT deliverable is generated from the blank master workbook bundled with the app:
strings.help.body.p9b: ; to use a different master, set the environment variable
strings.help.body.p9c: to point at your file. Only trimmed source builds without the bundled master report that a master is required when you click “Generate table”.
